app: **Some units cannot be at half-strength:** If a model’s W characteristic or a unit’s starting strength cannot be evenly divided in half, that model or unit cannot be at half-strength (but can be below half-strength as described above).
source: only in the less authoritative Wahapedia core rules (not in core, uru)
reason: Layout cross-reference. The Core Rules print the half-strength table to the right of this box ("as described on the right"); the app lists it above this line, so it keeps Wahapedia's wording "as described above". Every other word is the Core Rules text. PROPOSED: the coordinator decides whether the app keeps "above" or prints "on the right".
evidence: GW Core Rules PDF p86, box "Some units cannot be at half-strength": "(but can be below half-strength as described on the right)"; Wahapedia core rules 01.02.01 Starting Strength and Half-Strength: "(but can be below half-strength as described above)".

source: matches the less authoritative Wahapedia core rules, not the Core Rules: Your unit shoots using snap shooting (see below). | differs at "…nit shoots using snap shooting[.…]" vs source "…nit shoots using snap shooting[ (see below).…]"
reason: Layout cross-reference. The Core Rules end the effect with "(see below)", pointing at the Snap Shooting box printed under the stratagem; the owner's packet and Wahapedia print "Your unit shoots using snap shooting." and the app opens Snap Shooting from the bold term. PROPOSED: the coordinator decides whether to add "(see below)".
evidence: GW Core Rules PDF p57, 15.08 Fire Overwatch, EFFECT: "Your unit shoots using snap shooting (see below)."; verify/sources/packet/core-stratagems.txt p63 and Wahapedia core rules 15.08: "Your unit shoots using snap shooting."

app:
**Resolve a charge** with your unit (11.02). While doing so, before making the **charge roll**, you must select one of the following modes:
- **Leap to Defend:** When selecting **charge targets**, you can only select enemy units that made a **charge move** this phase and are within the **maximum distance**.
- **Into the Fray (+1CP):** When making the **charge roll**, if the result is greater than 6 (after modifiers), change it to 6. When selecting **charge targets**, you can select any enemy units that are within 6" of your unit and within the **maximum distance**.
source: Resolve a charge with your unit (11.02). While doing so, before making the charge roll, you must select one of the following modes: ▪ Leap to Defend: When selecting charge targets, you can only select enemy units that made a charge move this phase and are within the maximum distance. ▪ Into the Fray: ▫ When making the charge roll, if the result is greater than 6 (after modifiers), change it to 6. ▫ When selecting charge targets, you can select any enemy units that are within 6" of your unit and within the maximum distance. | differs at "…aximum distance. into the fray[ (+1cp): when making the charge roll, if…]" vs source "…aximum distance. into the fray[: when making the charge roll, if the re…]"
reason: Formatting of a layout element, no word changed: the Core Rules print the +1CP cost as a badge beside the Into the Fray mode and its two effects as sub-bullets; the app writes the cost as "(+1CP)" after the mode name and the two sub-bullets as one bullet (cpNote also says "Into the Fray +1CP").
evidence: GW Core Rules PDF p57, 15.11 Heroic Intervention: "Into the Fray:" with two sub-bullets and a "+1CP" badge; the packet (p64) prints the same layout.
